transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because my brain just kind of stalls out. I’ll have a test report or even a simple CAD note open for an hour, and I can’t figure out what the next sentence or checkbox is supposed to be.
Has this trouble focusing been a lifelong pattern for you, going back to childhood or school years, or is this something new that started more recently?
It’s newer. It started after I moved into the prototype-testing role, about a year and a month ago.
How has your sleep been over the past few weeks—are you having trouble falling or staying asleep, or waking up feeling unrested?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to my sleep lately.
Over the past month, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest or pleasure in things you'd normally enjoy?
Yeah. My miniature printer has had the same half-finished figure on it for months. Even yoga or walking in the woods just feels like another task now, not something I actually want to do.
You mentioned losing interest in things like your printer projects and yoga—how long has this loss of interest and low mood been going on?
Since I was moved into the prototype-testing role, so about a year and a month now.
Over this past year, have you noticed yourself worrying excessively about work performance or other things, feeling on edge, or having trouble controlling that worry?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed worrying like that specifically.
Besides the low mood and loss of interest, have you noticed changes in your energy level, appetite, or sleep, or feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt over this past year?
I keep replaying little mistakes I made in the lab. I tell myself it means I’m not just bad at the job, but bad as a person, and that I deserve whatever happens because of it.
Since this started about a year ago, has there been any stretch of two months or more where you felt back to your normal self, without the low mood or loss of interest?
No, I haven’t had a stretch like that. It’s been there since I moved into the prototype-testing role, about a year and a month ago.
When you think about deserving what happens to you, have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or that you would be better off dead?
Yeah. On my commute, I sometimes think it would be easier if I just didn’t arrive anywhere. And sometimes I get scared by the idea of steering off the road—I grip the wheel and pull over.
Over this past year, have you noticed a persistent drop in your energy level or feeling unusually fatigued most days, even after resting?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to my energy specifically.
